name: Owenism
summary: Owenism is the early British utopian socialism of Robert Owen and his followers. It holds that character is formed for people by their circumstances and education, blames private property, irrational religion and competition for social evil, and seeks to replace them with cooperative, communally owned villages, cooperative stores, labour exchanges and trade unions, reached by example and persuasion rather than revolution.
scope: Robert Owen's own doctrine and the Owenite movement of c.1813-1850 in Britain and the US (A New View of Society, the 1826 Declaration of Mental Independence, New Lanark, New Harmony, the labour exchange and the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union). It excludes later cooperative movements that dropped Owen's communitarian and anti-religious aims. Owen published little on modern issues, so most answers on them are low-confidence inferences from his principles.

sources.title: Robert Owen
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Character not made by the individual, rejection of religions, no corporal punishment, communities, unions, education, force opposed.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Owen's villages and New Lanark provided for health and care of all members, so a public duty of care is inferred; no healthcare scheme is documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Owen campaigned for better pay and conditions, but the remedy he offered was cooperation and labour notes, not wage law; inferred from his concern for workers' welfare.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Owenites rejected laissez-faire and competition, replacing exchange for profit with labour exchanges and cooperative stores.

public-ownership.rationale: Owenites wanted productive property held in common by communities; national state ownership of utilities is not their form, so only mild agreement is inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Owen aimed to end the dependence of the many on the wealthy few, but he sought change by community-building rather than taxation; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Owenites counted the trade union among their three core institutions and Owen led the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union in 1834.

property-fundamental.rationale: Owen named private or individual property as the first of three great evils and called for its destruction.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Owen's own remedy was to replace profit-making firms with cooperatives, though he did address Parliament on factory regulation; tighter regulation is inferred as a mild fit.

cut-welfare.rationale: Owenism rejected the Malthusian Poor Law reform and offered cooperative villages as pauper relief, so it opposed cutting relief.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative communities and cooperative production with common ownership by those who work in them were the Owenite programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented view; Owen's preventive, kindness-based approach to order and his stress on liberty of mind point mildly against surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Owenism never addressed drugs, and adherents' views on temperance and liberty would split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Owen demanded full freedom to attack religion and held that no one is to blame for opinions, so legal speech limits sit badly with it; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Owen was paternalist himself, yet he planned self-governing communities and expected change through gradual plans, so leader-led bypassing of politics is not an Owenite aim.

state-harmful.rationale: Owenism sought cooperative communities but not abolition of government; Owen consulted governments and wanted a 'Plan of Government' on preventive principles.

limit-guns.rationale: Owen's New Moral World aimed at ending violence by changing circumstances; gun control is inferred, not documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: Owen's preventive system aimed to remove the causes of crime and conflict rather than rely on force; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Owenites favoured freer marriage and sexual ethics, but adherents' views on prostitution are not documented in the sources read.

decide-locally.rationale: The Owenite model was self-governing communities of a few hundred to a few thousand, federated, which implies local decisions as a base.

rehabilitation.rationale: Owen held that character is made for, not by, the individual and opposed corporal punishment at New Lanark, so crime calls for reform, not retribution.

traditional-family.rationale: Owen attacked marriage founded on property and fostered communal child-rearing and infant schools, though private family apartments were kept in his communities.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Never addressed by Owenism; anachronistic, and its freer view of marriage gives no clear direction.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; Owenite sexual reformers differed on birth control, so no direction is inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Owen declared in 1817 that all religions were false and named irrational religion an evil, so a larger public role for religion runs against his creed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Owen's environmental view of character implies equality of human capacity, and race was not their focus.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Owen's principle that character is shaped by circumstances extends to gender by inference; his own texts here focus on class.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Owen's appeal was to a universal rational system and international communities, not to national tradition; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Owen expected change through well-arranged plans and example rather than upheaval, but he also called for a complete new system and rejected established religion and property.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's universal and international outlook, working in Scotland, England and the US, points against restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Owen proposed federations of communities and addressed governments worldwide, but never advocated an international authority as such.

free-trade.rationale: Owenites rejected laissez-faire political economy and wanted exchange by labour value; free trade as such is not documented, so inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Owen's New Moral World was universal and his plans were meant for all humanity; inferred opposition to national self-interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Owen held that force oppresses and that kindness corrects; military intervention is not addressed, so this is inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Owen's universalist vision and his emigrant projects imply open movement, but no explicit position is documented.

limit-growth.rationale: Owen welcomed machinery and productive power as the means of abundance if rightly directed, so growth limits are not an Owenite aim; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in Owenite texts, and adherents would be split between planning and technology.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Owen saw new productive power as capable of abolishing want if used under a rational social system; the problem was its social direction.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred only weakly from Owen's welcome of productive technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Owen looked to plans, example and persuasion, held that force oppresses, and Marx and Engels faulted the utopians for avoiding revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Owen thought a rational plan could be devised by enlightened people, yet he also wanted education of all; Owenites split between guidance and democracy.

central-planning.rationale: Owenites preferred planned cooperative communities, not a state-wide planned economy; they favoured planning at community scale and exchange by labour.

socialized-markets.rationale: Owenites accepted exchange through cooperative stores and labour exchanges owned by members, which partially matches, but they sought to supersede markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Never addressed by Owenism; Owenites aimed at common holding of land, not a tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Owen sought to end the dependence of the many on the wealthy, so curbs on inherited wealth are inferred, not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's communities guaranteed upkeep by labour and cooperation, not a cash grant.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Owen's 1817 memorial concerned machinery and unemployment, with no tariff stance documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Owen favoured some government involvement in the economy, but through funding cooperative villages rather than directing strategic industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Owenite goal was common ownership in cooperative communities, not wide distribution of private property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Owenites replaced money by hour-denominated labour notes at the Equitable Labour Exchange, and Owen's communities were meant to dispense with market wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The labour exchange issued its own notes, showing hostility to private money power, but the central bank question is not addressed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not an Owenite form; Owenites favoured voluntary unions and cooperatives over state-recognised wage bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Owenism had no party-state theory; Owenites joined the radical democratic movement and the Chartist current.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Owen courted royalty and aristocrats as patrons, but his rational society has no place for hereditary privilege; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Owen was at first apolitical and opposed some franchise radicals, though later Owenites joined the democratic movement that led to Chartism.

direct-votes.rationale: Not documented; community self-government is implied but no mechanism of direct lawmaking.

workers-councils.rationale: Owenites relied on cooperative societies and unions rather than councils as a basis of power; Owen avoided politics at first.

natural-rulers.rationale: Owen held that character comes from circumstances, not innate nature, so no group is born fit to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Owen held that force oppresses and that kindness corrects bad habits, so he opposed violence as a means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Owen's aim of a peaceful rational society and his rejection of force reject any virtue in war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Owen opposed all religions as false, so he would keep them out of the state; inferred, not documented as a constitutional principle.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Owen condemned irrational religion as one of three evils and thought all religions false, so scriptural law is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Owenites favoured common provision by communities and not commercial provision; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Owen's New Moral World aimed at peace and universal cooperation; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Owen's universal view of human nature as shaped by circumstance implies no ethnic basis for nations; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Owen sought cooperation with employers and rulers, and Marx and Engels criticised the utopians for rejecting class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Owen's communities shared goods communally, which suggests equality of conditions, but the sources read give no explicit statement.

civilizational-union.rationale: Owen's vision was universal and not tied to religion or civilization; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Owen blamed the competitive, individualist system for evil and built communities on cooperation and common interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cooperative communities stress mutual obligation, but Owen also stressed liberty of mind; adherents are not recorded on this ranking.

limit-population.rationale: Owenites rejected Malthus's Poor Law remedies and held that the world could feed more; birth control views split among later Owenites.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Owen thought industry's productive power, rightly organised, would bring abundance, so the problem is social order, not industry itself.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Owen welcomed productive power but wanted it governed by social plans; he did not favour disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen's idea of improving people was through education and surroundings, not technology.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; mild inference from Owen's community self-government and moral education.

restore-past-order.rationale: Owen looked forward to a New Moral World and called existing religion, marriage and property irrational, not worth restoring.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Owen proclaimed principles as demonstrable fact and tested them through experiments, which supports and opposes this item.

direct-action.rationale: Owenites used cooperative building, unions and later electoral politics; Owen's own method was persuasion and example.

means-match-ends.rationale: Owenites built the new society in miniature through cooperative stores and model communities, a prefigurative method.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Owen looked to machinery and science to deliver abundance and planned communities with advanced education.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Owen's communities combined agriculture and manufacturing, but he did not call for an end to specialisation; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Owen's communities supplied all members' needs from common stores, though labour-note schemes paid by labour; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Owenism replaced production for profit with exchange by labour and communities producing for their members' wants.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Owenism rested on the Ricardian labour theory of value and held that workers were deprived of the value of their labour by profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Owenism aimed at harmony among classes through peaceful community building and had no theory of class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Owenite villages farmed in common, as at Ralahine and New Harmony, though they were mixed agricultural-industrial communities.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Owen blamed competition and ignorance for conflict, but did not develop a theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Owen was no libertarian and expected governments to fund communities; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Owen defended freedom of thought and opinion while stating that conduct arises from circumstance; no liberty doctrine is documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Owen's collective communities rest on the group, but his 1826 oration stresses liberty of mind for each person; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Owen's pacific vision opposes compulsion to fight; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not documented; Owen's communal approach stresses participation, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Owenism opposed commercial competition as a social principle; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Owen held that people cannot be free to develop while deprived of food, education and care, which fits a material view of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Owen thought ruling ignorance, not a media class, was the cause of misery.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Owen's central claim is that character is formed by circumstance and training, which rejects innate group differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Owen favoured cooperative community federations and unions, but not family-based corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Owen's plan was voluntary communities, not total state direction of life, though he wanted the state to run education.

national-rebirth.rationale: Owen's New Moral World was a universal change in minds, not a national rebirth; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Owen's pacific outlook rejects conquest; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: No place in a rational cooperative society; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Owen's reforms aimed to improve workers' lives and his communities were voluntary associations, opposing bondage to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Owen treated his principles as demonstrable fact discoverable by reason, against relativism about knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Owen claimed a rational system founded on demonstrable facts, which suggests universal truths; but he also attacked inherited morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Owen saw a single harmonious interest of all under rational arrangements, rather than a balance of competing interests; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owenite cooperatives and communities were run by members, making democratic control of enterprises central.

school-vouchers.rationale: Owen wanted free state-provided or community education from infancy; vouchers for private choice are inferred as foreign to it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Owen's 1817 memorial urged public funds for work for the unemployed, which is compatible with spending to relieve distress.

economic-freedom.rationale: Owenites rejected laissez-faire and individual property as the basis of freedom; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Owen held that character is shaped by surroundings and relied on model communities and kindness rather than laws and punishments.

force-without-un.rationale: Owen's peaceful outlook points against force abroad; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Owen called his the Rational System, said religions were false, and based his claims on demonstrable fact.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Owen's universal outlook argues against restricting relief by nationality; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Owen's villages tied support to labour, but he opposed punitive Poor Law logic; adherents' stance on conditions is not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Owen appealed to employers and rulers to reform and was criticised by Marx and Engels for seeking cooperation with capitalists.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Owenites founded libraries and the Mechanics' Institutes, so destroying inherited institutions runs against their culture.

workers-nation.rationale: Owenism was internationalist in aim; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Owen's education was co-educational and his environmental view implies equal capacity; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Owenites' labour-exchange system rejected profit on exchange; a ban on interest is inferred, not documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Owen's view that circumstance forms character rules out racial hierarchy and it treats all as equally shaped by circumstance.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Owen believed rulers erred from ignorance rather than class interest, so he did not hold this view.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim foreign to Owen's view that ignorance and circumstance explain misery.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; Owenites did join the movement for wider suffrage.

national-mission.rationale: Owen pursued a universal mission, but not national imposition of a form of government; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Owenites were associated with women's and workers' rights reforms, so some structural view is inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Owen blamed rulers' ignorance rather than corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts Owen's emphasis on circumstance over innate nature and his benevolence.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not documented; inferred from Owen's concern with injustice and his hope for reform.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Owen wanted government to fund and plan cooperative communities and national education, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts Owen's environmental view of human character; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Owen held that no individual is to be blamed for a character formed for him, so all deserve kind and equal treatment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Owen planned model communities that would spread by example in any country; the Marxist doctrine is not his.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Owen asserted freedom to attack and leave religions; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Owen thought all religions false, so he would not have schools teach them, though New Lanark's own education was not described this way in sources read.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Owen praised the 1776 political independence as a step toward mental liberty, and Owenites later joined the democratic movement; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Owenites rejected mercantile competition between nations; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to Owen's benevolence and universalism; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Owen said force oppresses and kindness corrects, though he did not hold property rules as inviolable.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Owenism rejected competition in favour of cooperation as the principle of social order.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Owen defended freedom of opinion; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Owen's concern for the dependence of the many on the wealthy few is akin to a domination view, but he did not articulate it.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's 'Plan of Government' is described only as preventive.

vanguard-party.rationale: Owenites built cooperatives and unions of workers themselves; Marx and Engels faulted the utopians for not organising a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and cooperative villages were designed as relief for the poor and labouring classes.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic; Owenites favoured common ownership over individual home purchase.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Owen supported trade unions and led the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Owenites rejected Malthusian explanations and blamed social institutions and ignorance for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts Owen's belief that circumstances and education make people.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Owen defended liberty of mind and opposed force; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Owen's 'just price' roots suggest sympathy, but price controls are not documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: Owen demanded complete freedom of speech and press in the New Harmony Gazette; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian inference; not documented in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Owen proposed federations of communities, but supranational unions of states are not addressed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pacific and democratic leanings.

clerical-rule.rationale: Owen named irrational religion as one of three evils.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Owen was pacific but not revolutionary; no stance documented.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from democratic and communal self-government; not documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Peace aim suggests it; not documented.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Owenites favoured common holding, not individual home ownership for each family.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Owen's villages combined agriculture and industry in rural settings, but he valued New Lanark's industrial community too.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Owen prized education and founded schools and institutes; inferred rejection.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: His environmental theory of character implies equal capacity of peoples; but Owen thought his own system superior to existing customs.

death-penalty.rationale: Owen held that people are not to be blamed for a character formed for them and opposed punitive methods, so execution is rejected.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Owen stressed rational education from infancy and this is inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Owen held all religions to be false and based education on reason and demonstrable fact.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; freedom of belief supports it but Owen opposed religion itself.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Owen's oration demanded freedom from inherited prejudice and fixed custom of mind; he did not hold Mill's argument.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Owen presented political independence of 1776 as only a first step toward mental freedom, and economic change through common property as a further one.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Contrary to Owen's emphasis on liberty of mind.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from Owen's concern for the poor and his universalism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Owenites sought exchange by labour value rather than price stability under bankers; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Owen held that private property is an evil; the common interest should rule, and common property was the Owenite aim.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Owen opposed religions but wanted to educate people out of them, not to subordinate churches by law; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Self-governing communities with their own system fit this, but it is inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Owen called all religions false and rulers' errors due to ignorance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Owen's central doctrine is that character is formed for, not by, the individual by circumstances, and that proper early training can form any character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not documented; inferred from Owen's democratic and rational outlook.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen's plans concerned earthly cooperative communities, so no position can be drawn.

leader-cult.rationale: Owen himself was a revered founder, but he did not preach a cult of the leader as national embodiment.

land-redistribution.rationale: Owenites sought communal land holding, not giving estates to individual farmers; split between common and individual holding.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Owen openly attacked religion and demanded mental liberty.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the liberty of mind and freer outlook; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Owenites wanted labour notes, but monetary unions are not addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Owen's own emigrant community projects mean this has no clear answer.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Owen's circumstances-form-character thesis stresses surroundings, but it is not Marx's mode-of-production theory.

ban-cartels.rationale: Owenites opposed competition rather than seeking to preserve it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen's co-educational and egalitarian outlook gives no direction on quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Owen's villages were self-sufficient communities, but he did not advocate colonial trade blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Owen pioneered factory limits; a modern trade-standards analogue is inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Owen's communities relied on education in cooperative character, but also used labour notes; partial support.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Owen held that force oppresses and sought change through example and persuasion, so armed vanguards are foreign to him.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Owen attacked the dependence of the many on the privileged few, though he courted aristocrats; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from universalism and Owen's belief that circumstance forms character.

patriotic-education.rationale: Owen's education aimed at a rational, universal character; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen never addressed admissions or hiring preferences and his principles give no clear lean.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Owenite labour exchange issued its own notes against labour value, though not a state body.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Owen held that the existing system is irrational and must be replaced.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Owenism aimed at the whole working class; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts Owen's equal treatment of all and rejection of property as a basis of rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Owenites later joined democratic reform; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Owen's communities were run by community decisions, but veto is not documented.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; Owen preferred peaceful persuasion.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Owen petitioned Parliament but was cautious of politics; not documented.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Owen's kindness principle is general, but animals are not addressed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Owen's kindness principle was applied to people; animal use is not addressed in the sources read.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Owen's stress was on structural change, not charity of the privileged, though he appealed to employers.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Owen was at first apolitical and sought withdrawal into communities; later Owenites entered politics.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; Owen thought ignorance of both rulers and ruled was the cause of misery.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Owen's self-sufficient communities fit, but national development is not addressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; Owenism predates fascism by a century and offers no position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; Owenism predates both fascism and communism in power and offers no position.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Owen's equal-worth view implies it; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen never addressed public memorials, so no direction is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic; Owenism had no discussion of men's specific disadvantages.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anachronistic; Owen never addressed domestic violence statistics or policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Owen claimed universal rational principles; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Communal child-rearing and shared household work in Owen's plans imply recognising such work, but it is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Owen favoured communal child-rearing but kept family apartments.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Owenites sought common ownership, not protection of national firms; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Owen criticised marriage founded on property and mercenary motives, implying easy dissolution, though not stated in the sources read.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Owenism opposed individual property accumulation and relied on cooperative provision for all.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Common land holding in Owenite communities fits, though individual tenure rules are not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; discrimination law doctrine did not exist and Owenism gives no direction.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Owen opposed production for profit, which drives status consumption, but the sources read do not state this.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Owen's pacific outlook and his belief that force oppresses rule out arming insurgents abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Owen's pacific outlook rules out troops sent against an allied country's government.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from Owen's opposition to the wealthy few's power.

job-guarantee.rationale: Owen's 1817 memorial and Lanark report urged finding useful work for the unemployed, including through villages of cooperation.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; Owen sought peace through rational education, not through democratic institutions.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Owen's view that conduct reflects circumstances does not settle a duty of obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Owen's pacifism leans toward it, but his missionary approach to governments cuts the other way.

industrial-unions.rationale: The Grand National Consolidated Trades Union aimed to unite all trades, which fits broad industrial organisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims contradict Owen's view that ignorance and circumstance explain social ills.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Owen attacked marriage founded on property and mercenary motive and wanted it based on affection.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Owen's publicity of his plans and free press at New Harmony suggest it; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Owen's self-sufficient communities produced mainly for their own consumption.

informal-organisation.rationale: Owenites built formal societies, stores, exchanges and unions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's universalism gives no clear lean on constitutional versus international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Owen rejected religion as a social basis.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Owen's communities held production in common while families kept private apartments.

defeat-communism.rationale: Owen was a father of communal socialism but pacific; anachronistic.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Owenites favoured cooperative or common provision, not private providers.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and New Harmony proposed communities of roughly 500 to 3,000 people with common property as the remedy for poverty.

religion-illusion.rationale: Owen held that irrational religion was an evil born of false ideas about character and would give way to rational education; he did not describe it as consolation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Owen blamed private property and competition for social evil, though he valued industrial production and machinery as means to abundance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1826 Declaration treats property-based marriage as one of three evils, tying women's position to the property system.

socialized-care.rationale: Owen founded the New Lanark infant school and proposed state guardianship schools taking children from homes at age two.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Owen's universalist, rationalist outlook gives no place to linguistic purism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Owen never addressed treaties with internal nations; adherents have no documented position, so the answer is neutral.

majority-settlement.rationale: Owen's communities were voluntary and open, with a universal brotherhood outlook; steering a majority into minority regions is inferred as foreign to it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Owenites rejected capitalism and sought common property, which Marx classed as utopian socialism; they would not endorse rejecting both.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Owen's plans were universal and rested on common property and shared circumstance, not on any people's prior claim to land; inferred from this, as he never addressed the question.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He never addressed it (anachronistic); a committed adherent who traced evil to ignorance and rejected cruelty would reject denial of a mass atrocity, inferred from his principles.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Owen held that people are not responsible for how their character was formed and opposed punishment, so criminalising private conduct is inferred to be rejected; he did not discuss homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Owen sought change by example and persuasion and opposed force, so suppressing opponents is inferred to be rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Owen demanded freedom of speech on religion and attacked irrational religion as an evil, so punishing blasphemy or false worship contradicts his stance.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from his cooperative, non-coercive and anti-competitive principles; he did not write on colonial government.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Owen rejected all existing religions and force as a means; the duty is inferred to be rejected, and he did not address it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He opposed force and treated religion as an obstacle, so removing rulers by force over religious law is inferred to be rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Owenite communities were designed as self-governing cooperative villages and the movement built unions and cooperatives run by their members, though Owen himself was paternalistic.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Owenites joined class critique of property with early advocacy of women's equality in marriage and community life; the combined framing is inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from his view that character is formed by circumstance and should not be punished or blamed; the issue is anachronistic.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from his secular rationalism and humane opposition to needless suffering; he did not address the question.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Owen appealed to rulers and workers alike and to reason above party, so combining the best ideas across divides is inferred; the framing is anachronistic.

alienated-labor.rationale: Owen blamed the competitive factory system for degrading workers' character and sought cooperative labour, which is inferred to match this claim, though he did not use the term.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He rejected all religions equally as irrational and had a universalist outlook, so singling out Islam as incompatible is inferred to be rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He denounced irrational religion as one of the three great evils and traced authority to reason and circumstance, not to God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Owen's secular, anti-clerical stance implies religion should be kept out of state institutions; he did not discuss dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from his concern to protect workers from abuse by employers; the issue is anachronistic.

social-market-economy.rationale: Owenism rejected competition and the market in favour of cooperative communities and labour exchange, so a regulated market economy is not his model, though it is closer than laissez-faire.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Owen opposed force and war as products of bad circumstances and ignorance, so abolition is inferred to be congenial; he made no explicit proposal.

rich-first.rationale: Owen blamed competition and private property for social evil and sought common ownership so all would rise together, the opposite of letting some get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from his peaceful, internationalist outlook; blocs of rival powers postdate him.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Owen's plans rest on communal cooperation and education, not hereditary rank; no view on inherited office is documented, so this is inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Owenite labour exchange issued notes priced by labour cost, not profit, and the movement favoured cooperative self-help institutions; a user-owned bank is inferred from this.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Owen wrote before international lenders imposed conditions; his stress on self-supporting communities points to autonomy but adherents have no recorded position.

property-franchise.rationale: Owenites blamed private property for social evil and sought equal communal membership, so wealth as a qualification for voting is inferred to be rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Owenites urged equality for women in their communities, but nature-domination is a later ecological idea absent from the doctrine; no link is documented.

reification.rationale: Owenites blamed competition and profit for misery but did not use the later Marxist idea of social relations appearing as relations between things.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Owen held that private property and wealth shape circumstances and opinion, so formal freedoms looking hollow under unequal wealth is inferred; no statement on the press is documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Owen favoured rational, preventive government under settled rules and opposed arbitrary punishment, so rule by published law is inferred; the point is not stated directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: Owen's doctrine held that character is formed by circumstances and treated all people as equally formable, which leaves no ground for a racial limit on government.

online-participation.rationale: The internet postdates the movement; Owenite emphasis on direct community self-government gives no clear answer on online means.

open-government-data.rationale: Owen said nothing on public records; openness suits his rational, reasoned government but is only a weak inference.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Owen opposed all existing religions and attacked property-based marriage as one of three evils, so state limits on marriage across faiths conflict with his views.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Owen rejected religious division and held that no group is to blame for its character, and his cooperative stores served all members; shunning a religious minority's shops contradicts this.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Owenite communities governed themselves by member meetings, but choice by lot was not part of the movement and no position on it is documented.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Owen rejected all religions as irrational rather than seeking to reform them, so adherents would favour abandoning rather than reinterpreting doctrine; the statement is inferred as a mild disagree.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Owen blamed private property and competition for social evil and sought common ownership, so concentrated wealth as an engine of inequality and dependence is inferred as a danger.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in the 19th century; Owenites' tolerance and reform of punishment give no clear answer, so this is left neutral.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Owen was hostile to organised religion and wanted rational education, but he stressed freedom of conscience, so compelled state atheism is inferred as unwelcome.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Owen held that crime comes from circumstances and should be reformed rather than punished, so punitive prisons are rejected; but he did not call for abolishing all safeguards, an inference.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; Owen sought cooperative communities by persuasion and did not discuss minority power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Owen argued that private charity and poor relief leave the causes of poverty untouched and proposed communal planning in their place; inferred from his critique.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Owenites focused on communities and trade unions, not on electoral office.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; the idea is anachronistic, though Owenite community governance was participatory.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's concern was social reorganisation and he did not foresee extinction risk, so this is inferred as neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Owen supported equal rights for women in his communities and many Owenite women lectured; religious office is inferred as lower priority, so support is mild.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked marriage as then constituted and he advocated equality of the sexes, an inference for authority within marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Owen's universal, cooperative outlook, which saw all people's character as shaped by circumstances; not addressed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from his attack on private property and concern for workers' living conditions; rent law is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from Owen's opposition to private property and competition; patents are not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Owen's schools used drill and dance, but his aim was character formation, not national service, and he opposed national competition; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Owen's peaceable, cooperative philosophy.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Owen's opposition to war and competition between nations.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Owen's cosmopolitan humanism, which blamed bad circumstances rather than peoples.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Owenites held that labour is the source of value and tried to realise it through labour exchanges and hour-denominated labour notes.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Owen's peaceful, non-blaming doctrine that character is formed for the individual; no ruling on self-defence is documented.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Owen's cosmopolitan communitarianism, which put cooperative villages in place of national loyalties.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; Owen's environmentalism of character concerns formation of character, not sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; no documented Owenite position on this modern feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Owen's rejection of national competition and of religions that reward sacrifice; not directly sourced.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked irrational religion as a cause of social evil, and he sought reform by reason and example.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The statement concerns diaspora nationalism, which Owen did not address; his cosmopolitanism gives no clear lean.

culture-before-state.rationale: Owen held that education and character formation come first and reform follows; inferred from this for a nation's culture.

god-not-male.rationale: Owen rejected the religions of his day, so he would not endorse exclusively male language for God; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Owenites championed women's equality and rejected religious authority, so judging texts by women's humanity is inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Owen's cosmopolitan, anti-competitive outlook, which opposed ethnic or national privilege.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from Owen's cooperative, non-national communities, which are not defined by one people.

independent-unions.rationale: Owenites built trade unions and the Grand National Consolidated Trades Union as workers' own bodies and wanted no state direction, so independence is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Owenism sought cooperative communities run by their working members, so worker control of society is implied, though it sought it by example and not by seizing power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Owen's villages and cooperative communities provided common services for all members, implying communal provision of essentials.

second-chamber.rationale: Owen proposed unitary self-governing communities and no hereditary or privileged chamber, so a second chamber is inferred to be rejected.

municipal-property.rationale: Owen's communities held the means of production in common at the village level, as at New Harmony and the planned villages of co-operation in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Owen envisaged federations of cooperative villages with a federal coordinating body, an arrangement close to the statement.

family-wage.rationale: Owen at New Lanark improved pay and conditions for workers and families, so a living family wage is inferred; he sought to go beyond wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Owen believed in science and improvement of human welfare, so faster medical progress is inferred; he did not address regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Owen's faith in science and perfectibility of conditions suggests support, though he did not address ageing.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Owen did not address payments; the Owenite labour exchange issued its own notes outside state money, but that is a weak guide.

online-anonymity.rationale: Owen did not address online anonymity; no principle supports a firm answer.

person-over-state.rationale: Owen held that society exists to form good character and happiness of every person, so the person as an end rather than a means is implied.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Owen's Declaration of Mental Independence attacked religion as one of three great evils and held that character is formed by circumstances, so a spiritual nature is rejected as stated.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Owen's plans were for self-governing communities, so autonomy resting on revocable grants is inferred to be rejected.

gm-crops.rationale: Owen believed in applying science to improve production and welfare, so GM crops are inferred to be acceptable; anachronistic.

dense-cities.rationale: Owen planned compact communities of roughly 1,000 to 1,500 people, so compact settlement is inferred; not about modern cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Owen held that character is formed by circumstances and not by race, and he sought universal cooperation, so race-based organising is inferred to be rejected.

racial-pride.rationale: Owen's universal-brotherhood outlook and view that character is made by circumstances imply racial pride has no basis; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Owen was a committed advocate of peace and cooperation, so wars of aggression are inferred to be rejected, though he did not address defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Owen was a cosmopolitan who held character is formed by circumstances and aimed at a universal society of cooperative villages, so national identity from language is inferred as foreign to his outlook.

communal-electorates.rationale: Owen attacked sectarian religion as a cause of social evil and sought a common cooperative order, so religiously separate electorates are inferred to be opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Owenism blamed ignorance and bad institutions, not foreign plots, and saw nations as potential cooperators; no such claim is documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Owen championed free education from infancy for forming character, from which free public higher education is inferred; he never addressed colleges directly.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Owen never addressed pollution or resource pricing; his communal-ownership principles and his distrust of market mechanisms pull in different directions.

future-generations.rationale: Owen aimed at a permanently better society formed through the education of the young, so a duty to later generations is inferred; environmental stewardship is not documented.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Owenites argued for sexual equality and cooperation, but no source shows them ascribing distinct values to women, and adherents are inferred to be split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Owen opposed war and competition as products of a bad social system and expected cooperative communities to remove its causes, so reducing armaments is inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Owen urged open appeals to governments and publics and rejected secrecy as a mark of the irrational system, so open diplomacy is inferred; he did not address treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Owen never addressed international capital flows, and his cooperative and anti-competition principles give no clear direction on border controls.

missingStatements.text: No person should be blamed or punished as if they had made their own character, since it is formed for them by circumstances.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen drew the conclusion that character is made not by but for the individual and that blame is therefore misplaced; the bank asks about environment and punishment but not this moral conclusion.

missingStatements.text: Goods should be exchanged at a value measured by the hours of labour put into them, using labour notes in place of money.
missingStatements.rationale: The Owenite National Equitable Labour Exchange issued hour-denominated labour notes; no statement captures labour-time money.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow exchange mechanism; its underlying aims are covered by abolish-money-wages, production-for-use and public-money-creation.

missingStatements.text: Society should be reorganised into self-governing cooperative villages that hold their property in common.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen's Lanark report and New Harmony proposed communities of roughly 500 to 3,000 people with common property as the remedy for poverty.

missingStatements.text: Children should be educated from infancy in free schools aimed at forming their character.
missingStatements.rationale: Owen founded the New Lanark infant school and Institute for the Formation of Character, and proposed state guardianship schools.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal today and a policy detail; the character-formation premise is covered by character-from-environment.

notes: Owen's own views and later Owenite politics differed: Owen was apolitical and wary of franchise radicals, while later Owenites joined the democratic reform movement that led to Chartism. Owen's account of marriage and sex is thinly sourced here (only the 1826 oration), so family and sexuality answers are low confidence.
